diagnosis.root_cause: A shared splitter segment on EPON0/6 has failed, taking multiple ONUs offline while other ONUs on the same PON port remain online. The affected subscriber is one of the definite offline ONUs.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds successfully with online:0, so the subscriber is definitively offline rather than merely unmonitored.
The same port has four definite offline ONUs at indices 15, 16, 19, 20, and 46, while indices 8, 13, 49, and 57 remain online.
Two or more offline ONUs with surviving peers on the same port places the failure boundary inside the port and identifies a splitter failure.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, and its CPU, memory, and temperature are normal, ruling out an OLT-wide failure.
The router heartbeat is healthy, and the expected customer VLAN 1016 is present and correct.
RADIUS authentication and CRM line identity are consistent, with only one session in the last 24 hours, so authentication is not causing the outage.

Historical RX power was stable around -22.4 to -23.1 dBm, TX power stayed near +2.3 dBm, distance stayed constant at 294 m, and TX bias remained healthy; there is no evidence of fibre, laser, or distance degradation for this ONU.
The OLT-wide offline total of 25 is above the normal background estimate, but the direct mixed online/offline port evidence is stronger and specifically identifies a shared failure on EPON0/6.

remediation.action: Dispatch field technicians to inspect and replace or repair the splitter and associated fibre connections serving the affected EPON0/6 customers. Verify ONU registration and optical levels after repair, then clear and recheck the mass-offline alarm.

ground_truth.root_cause: Eleven of the thirty-four customers on EPON0/6 lost service within the same minute while the remaining twenty-three continue normally. A shared downstream splitter branch has failed; the PON port itself is still working.
expected_reasoning: Probing EPON0/6 shows eleven ONUs offline and twenty-three still online with normal RX and TX
Because part of the port is still serving, the port optics and feeder fibre are working
The eleven failures occurred within the same minute, which rules out unrelated individual faults
A simultaneous partial loss on a working port indicates a shared element downstream of the port
That element is a splitter branch serving those eleven customers
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory and temperature are all normal, so the OLT is not involved
The health check still reports the OLT healthy, which is correct here but only because the port has surviving ONUs
PON port traffic has fallen but not collapsed, consistent with losing a third of the port
The affected set is the eleven, not the whole port
distractors: Eleven simultaneous outages could be read as a PON port failure if the surviving ONUs are not probed
The OLT health check reports healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The affected ONU indexes are not contiguous, obscuring the shared branch
